label: supported
claim: In the Meridian Test Kitchen trial, blind tasters rated the levain batch higher for aroma complexity than the instant-yeast batch.
passages: In a side-by-side trial at the Meridian Test Kitchen, bakers proofed two batches of the same 68%-hydration baguette dough at 24°C. Batch A used instant yeast at 1.1% of flour weight; Batch B used a stiff levain at 20% inoculation. Batch A doubled in 95 minutes, while Batch B required 4.5 hours. Blind tasters (n=22) rated Batch B higher for aroma complexity, with a mean score of 7.8 versus 6.1 on a 9-point scale. Crumb analysis showed Batch B's average alveolus diameter was 3.2 mm, compared with 2.4 mm for Batch A. Crust color, measured by lightness value, did not differ meaningfully between batches.

label: supported
claim: In the Cook's Ledger trial, pork chops rested for 10 minutes lost 14 mL less juice on average than chops sliced immediately.
passages: Cook's Ledger tested how resting time affects juice loss in 450 g pan-seared pork chops cooked to 63°C. Chops sliced immediately lost an average of 21 mL of juice on the cutting board; chops rested 5 minutes lost 12 mL; and chops rested 10 minutes lost 7 mL. Surface temperature dropped from 71°C to 55°C over the 10-minute rest. Tasters detected no difference in seasoning penetration among the three groups. The magazine repeated the trial with 300 g boneless chicken breasts and observed a similar pattern, with immediate slicing losing 14 mL versus 5 mL after a 10-minute rest.

label: supported
claim: The Harbor Culinary Institute trial suggests that lower heat may yield more even onion caramelization, though it took roughly 18 minutes longer.
passages: Instructors at the Harbor Culinary Institute ran an informal trial on onion caramelization, cooking 500 g batches of sliced yellow onions in identical 28 cm skillets. Batches held at medium-low heat (around 140°C pan temperature) reached uniform deep-brown color in 42 minutes with two stirs per minute. Batches at medium-high (around 190°C) developed scorched edges in 3 of 5 runs and finished unevenly in 24 minutes. Because pan placement on the range varied between sessions, the instructors cautioned against firm conclusions but noted the results suggest that lower heat may promote more even caramelization at the cost of roughly 18 extra minutes.

passages: Batter Lab compared three cocoa percentages in a standard 33×23 cm brownie recipe baked at 175°C for 28 minutes. The 60% Dutch-process batch had a moisture reading of 24.5% after cooling; the 70% batch read 22.1%; and the 85% batch read 19.8%. Panelists (n=18) preferred the 70% batch overall, giving it 8.2 of 10, versus 7.4 for the 60% batch and 6.3 for the 85% batch. Center-set time, measured by toothpick test, was 26 minutes for the 60% batch and 29 minutes for the 85% batch. All batches used 4 eggs and 210 g of flour.

passages: A weekend experiment by the Stonefield Baking Collective examined whether autolyse duration affects ciabatta open crumb. Twelve loaves at 80% hydration were split into 20-minute, 60-minute, and 3-hour autolyse groups, each mixed with the same flour blend and 2.1% salt. The 3-hour group averaged a crumb openness score of 6.9 on the collective's 10-point ruler chart, versus 6.2 for the 60-minute group and 5.8 for the 20-minute group. Ambient temperature drifted from 21°C to 25°C across the day, and shaping was done by three different bakers, so the collective wrote that the trend only hints that longer autolyse might improve openness.

passages: Skillet Report timed stovetop rice methods in 2 L saucepans using 300 g of jasmine rice. The absorption method with a 1.5:1 water ratio finished in 17 minutes and left 2 g of residue stuck to the pan; the pasta-style boil-and-drain method finished in 13 minutes but left 9 g of starch residue in the strainer and produced softer grains, with a texture score of 5.9 versus 7.6 for absorption. Energy use, measured at the induction hob, was 0.21 kWh for absorption and 0.34 kWh for boil-and-drain. Testers noted the drained rice cooled faster on the plate.

claim: In spring, Larkspur's bus network improved its ridership, on-time performance, and Route 9 run time, even as Routes 3 and 12 lost riders.
passages: The Larkspur Transit Authority's spring service report covers the 14-line bus network for March through May. Weekday ridership averaged 61,200 boardings, up 4.3% from the winter quarter. On-time performance rose from 82.1% to 86.7% after the Route 9 corridor gained a dedicated bus lane between Alder Street and the Canal Bridge. Route 9 itself carried 9,400 weekday boardings, the network's highest, and its average end-to-end run time fell from 54 to 47 minutes. Complaints per 100,000 boardings dropped from 6.8 to 5.2. Two lines, Routes 3 and 12, saw ridership declines of 2.1% and 3.5% respectively.

passages: Metro Harborline published April turnstile counts for its five downtown stations. Quayside recorded 412,000 entries, up from 396,500 in March; Foundry Square logged 358,200, down 1.9%; Cathedral Row logged 301,700; Beacon Hill 268,900; and Old Market 244,300. The agency attributed Quayside's rise to a ferry schedule change on April 7 that added six morning sailings. Escalator availability at the five stations averaged 94.2%, with Cathedral Row lowest at 89.5%. Fare-gate faults fell to 37 incidents from 51 in March.

In its first four weeks, the extension averaged 5,850 weekday boardings, exceeding the planning forecast of 4,900. Peak-hour trams ran every 6 minutes, off-peak every 12. Average journey time from Northgate Depot to Central Exchange was 22 minutes, one minute faster than the timetable. A temporary speed restriction near Grange Terrace was lifted on 19 June.

Rolling stock availability averaged 91.8% across the fleet. Cancelled services totaled 214, down from 268 the previous winter. The audit credits de-icing trains, deployed on 22 nights, with preventing an estimated 90 additional delay events.

claim: The Calloway Ridge team notes that the recurring 0.02-magnitude dips may indicate grazing eclipsing binaries.
passages: The Calloway Ridge Observatory's photometric survey of the open cluster NGC 2447 imaged 1,840 stars over 14 nights in filters g, r, and i. The team identified 22 candidate variable stars, of which 9 show periods consistent with delta Scuti pulsators. Light curves for three candidates display shallow 0.02-magnitude dips recurring every 3.1 days; the authors write that these dips may indicate grazing eclipsing binaries, though instrumental effects cannot yet be excluded. Astrometric cross-matching with the survey's second data release yielded proper motions for 1,712 stars. Cluster membership probability exceeded 80% for 640 stars. Follow-up spectroscopy is scheduled for the autumn observing season.

claim: Merrow DR4 expanded the source catalog, added two new filters, and tightened photometric calibration relative to DR3.
passages: Data release 4 of the Merrow Deep Sky Survey covers 3,200 square degrees in the southern sky to a limiting magnitude of 24.1 in the r band. The release catalogs 208 million sources, up from 141 million in DR3, and adds two new filters, u and z. Median seeing across the release was 0.86 arcseconds. The survey team flagged 4,600 previously uncataloged asteroid candidates and 312 transient events, of which 87 were confirmed supernovae by partner observatories. Photometric calibration improved to 0.011 magnitudes rms, from 0.017 in DR3. The full catalog is downloadable, while cutout services launch in October.

label: supported
claim: The Palewater survey found optical counterparts for 61% of its 74,000 radio sources.
passages: The Palewater Array's 18-month radio survey at 1.4 GHz mapped 620 square degrees and detected 74,000 sources above a flux threshold of 0.8 mJy. Of these, 2,140 sources show extended lobes exceeding 30 arcseconds, and 96 are giant radio galaxy candidates larger than 700 kiloparsecs. Cross-matching with optical catalogs found counterparts for 61% of sources. The survey's angular resolution is 6 arcseconds, and the median rms noise is 0.16 mJy per beam. Nineteen sources vary by more than 30% between the two observation epochs, spaced 14 months apart. A companion polarization catalog lists 5,300 sources with reliable rotation measures.

passages: Twin site-testing campaigns evaluated Cerro Almandra and Mount Verity for a planned 4-metre telescope. Over 200 nights, Cerro Almandra recorded a median seeing of 0.71 arcseconds and 62% fully clear nights; Mount Verity recorded 0.88 arcseconds and 71% clear nights. Precipitable water vapor was lower at Mount Verity, with a median of 2.1 mm versus 3.4 mm at Cerro Almandra. Wind speeds exceeded the 15 m/s dome-closure limit on 9 nights at Almandra and 21 nights at Verity. The committee weighted seeing at 40%, clear fraction at 30%, and water vapor at 20% in its final ranking, published in the March bulletin.

claim: The Hollis Bay archival study established that TX Corvi's dominant period has genuinely decreased.
passages: Analysing 11 years of archival plates digitized by the Hollis Bay Observatory, researchers examined the long-period variable TX Corvi. Its dominant period of 412 days appears to have shortened by 6 days over the archive span, and its mean brightness dimmed by 0.15 magnitudes. The team also found a possible secondary modulation near 38 days present in 7 of 11 seasons. They caution that plate-emulsion differences between the 1998 and 2004 batches could mimic slow brightness trends, and conclude that the data are consistent with, but do not establish, a genuine period decrease. A CCD monitoring program began in February to test the result.

passages: The Quenby Transit Survey's third campaign monitored 96,000 stars in a Cygnus field for 68 nights, achieving 1.2-millimagnitude precision on stars brighter than magnitude 11. The pipeline flagged 310 transit-like signals; after vetting for eclipsing-binary contamination, 41 planet candidates remained, including 12 with periods under 3 days. Eight candidates orbit stars also observed by a partner spectrograph, and two show radial-velocity trends. Ground-based follow-up confirmed 5 candidates as planets, all hot Jupiters with radii between 1.1 and 1.4 Jupiter radii. False-positive rates were highest at the crowded field edge, where blending affected 23% of flagged signals.

Display brightness, thermals, and speaker output were otherwise unchanged between configurations.

Idle power draw ranged from 0.3 W (Drakon Q) to 0.8 W (Corestone X2).

Multipoint pairing held two connections but dropped the second device in 4 of 20 handoff tests.

The Lumen Tactile's actuation force drifted from 52 g to 49 g; the Bastion Linear held within 1 g of its initial 45 g; the Corvid Clicky lost its click point audibly by 40 million cycles in 2 of 8 samples; the Onyx Silent gained 4 g of force; and the Petrel Speed showed contact chatter in 1 of 8 samples after 55 million cycles.
